title: Decoding the Secrets of Egyptian Hieroglyphs
description:
S01 E02 — The Ancient Egyptian Alphabet
Learning the hieroglyphic alphabet; how to write and position each hieroglyph, including a stylized hand, a horned viper and two hieroglyphs for which English does not have a letter; transcribing one's name from English to ancient Egyptian.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E01 — Paleolithic Cave Art of Spain and France
The oldest paintings in the world, in the extraordinary cave art of Altamira, Lascaux, and Chauvet.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E02 — The Taj Mahal of Agra
Learning about the builder of Taj, the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan, and his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal, for whom it was built.

title: Masters of War: History's Greatest Strategic Thinkers
description:
S01 E01 — Why Strategy Matters
If war is a gamble, then a strategy is key to success; a survey of why strategy is important; looking at World War II's "Operation Torch" as a case study for how the military should be used as an instrument of policy.

title: Masters of War: History's Greatest Strategic Thinkers
description:
S01 E02 — Thucydides On Strategy
A systematic look at what makes Thucydides perhaps history's first great strategist; his analysis of the Peloponnesian War; the political origins of the war; the Spartan and Athenian leadership; the social and moral implications of war.

title: History's Great Military Blunders and the Lessons They Teach
description:
S01 E01 — Petersburg: Union Digs Its Own Grave - 1864
Following the chain of events that led to the Civil War's ill-fated Battle of the Crater; what can happen in warfare when a plan goes awry due to various factors; the phenomenon of military blunders and what they can teach people.

title: History's Great Military Blunders and the Lessons They Teach
description:
S01 E02 — Syracuse: Athens's Second Front - 413 B.C.
From initiating a second front with a new enemy to dividing supreme command among multiple generals; how failures of decision-making and leadership spelled disaster for the Greek city state of Athens in the outcome of the Peloponnesian War.

title: The Persian Empire
description:
S01 E01 — Rethinking the Persian Empire
Cyrus, Darius and Xerxes; these Persian kings are sometimes stereotyped as one-dimensional despots in Greek histories; the truth about the Achaemenid Persian Empire; an empire that stretches from Egypt and Asia Minor, all the way to the Indus Valley.

title: The Persian Empire
description:
S01 E02 — Questioning the Sources
Greek historians provide valuable information about the Persian Empire; the Greek perspective is often negatively biased; archaeology uncovers inscriptions, administrative tablets and other documents that let the Persians speak for themselves.

title: Understanding Russia: A Cultural History
description:
S01 E01 — A Russian Past, the Putin Future
The heart of Russian history and culture; examining many themes; the enormity of Russia's geography; its desire for power; its search for an organic cultural identity; exploring the beginnings of Russia in the land known as Rus'.

title: Understanding Russia: A Cultural History
description:
S01 E02 — Ivan the Terrible's 500-Year Reign
Ivan the Terrible's reign is a cultural and historical symbol of Russian leadership; how he uses cultural symbols to create a spectacle of autocracy; knowing to what extent he sets the standard for subsequent centuries of the Russian leadership.

title: Herodotus: The Father of History
description:
S01 E01 — Herodotus and History
Identifying key issues of definition and terminology; explaining what is known about the life of Herodotus; background on the ancient Greek world; summarizing the momentous events, particularly the Persian Wars, that spur Herodotus to write.

title: Herodotus: The Father of History
description:
S01 E02 — "Inquiry" and the Birth of History
Herodotus is not the first Greek to write about the past; knowing makes him original; how he explains, in the very first sentence of his work and one that richly rewards close reading, the what, why and how of his monumental effort.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E01 — Bearing Off: The Story of Backgammon
During the Third Crusade, the European soldiers spend the winter playing the ancient game of Tables, which would evolve into backgammon by the 20th century.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E02 — Senet: Egypt's Game of the Afterlife
Unearthed artifacts from King Tutankhamun's tomb include Senet boards. Historians study the hieroglyphs and investigate the abrupt disappearance of this ancient Egyptian game.

title: Decoding the Secrets of Egyptian Hieroglyphs
description:
S01 E01 — Why Egypt Needed Hieroglyphs
Understanding why Ancient Egypt has to invent some form of writing; central to this introduction is a study of the Narmer Palette; its writing sets standards and conventions that would be followed for 3,000 years.

title: Decoding the Secrets of Egyptian Hieroglyphs
description:
S01 E02 — The Ancient Egyptian Alphabet
Learning the hieroglyphic alphabet; how to write and position each hieroglyph, including a stylized hand, a horned viper and two hieroglyphs for which English does not have a letter; transcribing one's name from English to ancient Egyptian.

description:
S01 E01 — Paleolithic Cave Art of Spain and France
The oldest paintings in the world, in the extraordinary cave art of Altamira, Lascaux, and Chauvet.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E02 — The Taj Mahal of Agra
Learning about the builder of Taj, the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan, and his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal, for whom it was built.

title: Masters of War: History's Greatest Strategic Thinkers
description:
S01 E02 — Thucydides On Strategy
A systematic look at what makes Thucydides perhaps history's first great strategist; his analysis of the Peloponnesian War; the political origins of the war; the Spartan and Athenian leadership; the social and moral implications of war.

title: Notorious London: A City Tour
description:
S01 E01 — Oscar Wilde's Decadent London
London when it is home to Oscar Wilde at the close of the 19th century; the details of Wilde's trial for indecency; the way London society is structured; how immense wealth and privilege, for some, leaves its imprint on the city and its history.

title: Notorious London: A City Tour
description:
S01 E02 — St. Paul's Cathedral in Faith, Fire, and Sin
St. Paul's Cathedral has overlooked London from a high point in the city for generations; the history of this church that has been much more than a place of worship; it has survived fire and the ravages of war; episodes from the cathedral's past.

title: Notorious London: A City Tour
description:
S01 E03 — Getting Blitzed at London's Café de Paris
An evening in March 1941, when the Café de Paris is destroyed in the Blitz; the history of the café; how its destruction reflects the horrors of wartime London; the resiliency of the citizens who keep calm and carry on under the threat of war.

title: Notorious London: A City Tour
description:
S01 E04 — On Carnaby Street during the Swinging '60s
Carnaby Street emerges in the 17th century; a symbol of social change in the 1960s; its history; it becomes a magnet for trendsetters and youth culture in post-war London; why these changes are embraced by some and seen as a threat by others.

title: Notorious London: A City Tour
description:
S01 E05 — A History of Infamy in the Tower of London
The history of the Tower of London and its many roles; fortress, royal residence; military garrison; zoo and, perhaps most notably, prison; days of William the Conqueror; the Victorian era; this structure plays a crucial part in London's history.

title: Notorious London: A City Tour
description:
S01 E06 — Underground Catholics of Protestant London
The Protestant Reformation of her father Henry VIII's reign; Elizabeth I and her successor James I rule over an England torn by religious controversy; their rules are characterized by many conspiracies; the history of religious persecution in London.

title: Notorious London: A City Tour
description:
S01 E07 — Wicked Fun at the Vauxhall Pleasure Gardens
Popular with the aristocracy and the middle classes; the Vauxhall Pleasure Gardens are 12 acres of woods and gravel walks on the South Bank of the Thames; the stories of social interaction, pleasure, and danger that abound around this public place.

title: Notorious London: A City Tour
description:
S01 E08 — Taking the Dead Man's Path to Tyburn Tree
The trial and execution of Jack Sheppard in 1724; Jack's story highlights the public display of state power and the nature of public life in 18th-century London; Jack Sheppard meets an ignominious end; the haves and the have-nots of London's past.

title: The Real History of Dracula
description:
S01 E01 — Why Dracula Frightens and Seduces Us
Exploring the roots of the vampire in European folklore that precedes Dracula's creation.

title: The Real History of Dracula
description:
S01 E02 — Surprises from Bram Stoker's Dracula
Examining Dracula's role in shaping Western culture.

title: The Real History of Dracula
description:
S01 E03 — Vampires and Bloodlust before Dracula
Examining the literary and historical sources influencing Stoker's creation of Dracula.

title: The Real History of Dracula
description:
S01 E04 — How Dracula Became a Count
Exploring stoker's choice for an elegant and sophisticated vampire count.

title: The Real History of Dracula
description:
S01 E05 — Vampire Romance On-Screen
Exploring the romantic evolution of modern vampires.

title: The Real History of Dracula
description:
S01 E06 — Why Dracula and Disease Travel Together
The impact of vampire narratives on real-world discourse of disease.

title: The Real History of Dracula
description:
S01 E07 — The Vampiric Threat from Abroad
Dracula's role in the Victorian sub-genre - Analyzing how themes of foreign invasion shape the gothic narrative and its modern adaptations.

title: The Real History of Dracula
description:
S01 E08 — How to Kill a Vampire
The evolution of vampire-fighting methods through the ages.

title: Exploring the Mayan World
description:
S01 E01 — Mérida
A trip to Mérida, the capital of the Yucatán; visiting a factory hosting the revival of an industry that made the Yucatán rich more than 100 years ago; the mansions lining Mérida's Paseo de Mont; shopping for the perfect hammock and guayabera shirt.

title: Exploring the Mayan World
description:
S01 E02 — Chichén Itzá
Traveling to Izamal, the "yellow city" named after the Maya sky god; touring the city's history, including a walk through the Convent of St. Anthony of Padua; venturing to Chichen Itza; looking at the achievements of Maya architecture.

title: Exploring the Mayan World
description:
S01 E03 — Ek' Balam
A trip to Valladolid and Ek' Balam, two places in the Yucatan; the first offers travelers a chance to see a traditional agave distillery and an all-female troop of competitive horseback riders; the second is the ruins of what was once a Maya capital.

title: Exploring the Mayan World
description:
S01 E04 — Tihosuco
Accompanying Dr. Barnhart as he writes his name in Maya hieroglyphs; talking to howler monkeys; plunging into a geological cathedral; a journey to Tihosuco, home to an episode of an oppressed people fighting for their independence.

title: Exploring the Mayan World
description:
S01 E05 — Mayapán
Exploring the history and culture of Mayapan and its surrounding region; the destruction of sacred Maya codices during public acts of faith held by the Spanish friar Diego de Landa; sampling dishes of grilled pork and ground pumpkin seeds.

title: Exploring the Mayan World
description:
S01 E06 — Uxmal
Discovering what makes Uxmal a marvel of Maya urban planning; Dr. Barnhart explores archeological features, including the Pyramid of the Dwarf, the Palace of the Governors and the Nunnery Quadrangle; exploring the Loltun Caves.

title: Exploring the Mayan World
description:
S01 E07 — Celestún
Looking at Kabah, where one will find over 200 faces of Chaac the rain god and a rare example of literate public art; visiting Becal, famous for producing some of the best jipijapas in the Yucatán; taking a trip to the Celestun biosphere.

title: Exploring the Mayan World
description:
S01 E08 — Labná
Labna is an architectural wonder crowned by three buildings, which are the Palacio, the El Mirador pyramid and the Labna Arch; decoding the cultural messages in these famous works; traveling back to Merida.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E01 — The Discoveries and Their Significance
Learning about the Dead Sea Scrolls and their discovery; ancient Judaism and early Christianity prior to the scrolls; the uncovering of the scrolls and how they alter one's understanding of every aspect of the historical period of their creation.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E02 — The First Seven Scrolls
Diving into a tale of excitement and adventure and discovering more about how scholars gain access to the first seven scrolls discovered at Qumran; what they find when they begin to translate the extraordinary initial discoveries.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E03 — Opening and Reading the First Scroll
Immersing into the text of the scrolls, starting with the scroll known as the Community Rule or Manual of Discipline; the important text that gives one the first insight into the community and theology of the scrolls' creators and guardians.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E04 — The Historical Backdrop of Ancient Judaism
Examining history prior to the scrolls, beginning with the biblical period and moving to the Maccabean revolt; the arrival of the Romans; King Herod's reign; the life of Jesus; the Zealot revolt; the destruction of Jerusalem and the fall of Masada.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E05 — The Rise of the Jewish Sects
Jewish sectarianism in late antiquity; focusing on the Sadducees, Pharisees, Essenes and Zealots through Josephus, the Jewish philosopher Philo and the authors of the New Testament books; the later rabbis; Roman polymath Pliny the Elder.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E06 — The Dead Sea Site of the Qumran Sect
Visiting the isolated region of Qumran's caves; learning how archeological excavations of a nearby ruin help scholars form the most accepted hypothesis of who writes the scrolls and why the scrolls are deposited in the caves.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E07 — The Emergence of the Rabbinic System
Stepping forward in time and examining some later rabbinic texts from the third century; the rise of the rabbinical tradition; vital perspectives on the composition of the Dead Sea Scrolls.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E08 — A Dead Sea Scroll from Medieval Cairo
Two copies of the Damascus Document are discovered in a Cairo synagogue in the 1890s; although the copies are medieval, the texts are believed to be ancient, a conclusion later confirmed when fragments of the same texts are found at Qumran.

Learning about the Dead Sea Scrolls and their discovery; ancient Judaism and early Christianity prior to the scrolls; the uncovering of the scrolls and how they alter one's understanding of every aspect of the historical period of their creation.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E02 — The First Seven Scrolls
Diving into a tale of excitement and adventure and discovering more about how scholars gain access to the first seven scrolls discovered at Qumran; what they find when they begin to translate the extraordinary initial discoveries.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E03 — Opening and Reading the First Scroll
Immersing into the text of the scrolls, starting with the scroll known as the Community Rule or Manual of Discipline; the important text that gives one the first insight into the community and theology of the scrolls' creators and guardians.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E04 — The Historical Backdrop of Ancient Judaism
Examining history prior to the scrolls, beginning with the biblical period and moving to the Maccabean revolt; the arrival of the Romans; King Herod's reign; the life of Jesus; the Zealot revolt; the destruction of Jerusalem and the fall of Masada.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E05 — The Rise of the Jewish Sects
Jewish sectarianism in late antiquity; focusing on the Sadducees, Pharisees, Essenes and Zealots through Josephus, the Jewish philosopher Philo and the authors of the New Testament books; the later rabbis; Roman polymath Pliny the Elder.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E06 — The Dead Sea Site of the Qumran Sect
Visiting the isolated region of Qumran's caves; learning how archeological excavations of a nearby ruin help scholars form the most accepted hypothesis of who writes the scrolls and why the scrolls are deposited in the caves.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E07 — The Emergence of the Rabbinic System
Stepping forward in time and examining some later rabbinic texts from the third century; the rise of the rabbinical tradition; vital perspectives on the composition of the Dead Sea Scrolls.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E08 — A Dead Sea Scroll from Medieval Cairo
Two copies of the Damascus Document are discovered in a Cairo synagogue in the 1890s; although the copies are medieval, the texts are believed to be ancient, a conclusion later confirmed when fragments of the same texts are found at Qumran.

title: The Middle Ages Around the World
description:
S01 E01 — Medieval Beginnings: The Fall of Empires
Turbulent events that marked the beginning of the Middle Ages.

title: The Middle Ages Around the World
description:
S01 E02 — Constantinople, Aksum, and Tang China
Joyce E. Salisbury provides insight into the relationship between sophisticated medieval cities and their supporters.

title: The Middle Ages Around the World
description:
S01 E03 — The Rise of Islam and Europe's Knights
The expansion of Islam and how people fared under Muslim rule.

title: The Middle Ages Around the World
description:
S01 E04 — Creating an Islamic Culture
The cultural transformations that Muslim rule brought to its domains.

title: The Vikings
description:
S01 E01 — The Vikings in Medieval History
Hostile Christian sources demonize the Vikings; Muslim accounts render them exotic; revisionist historians belittle the Norse raids; archeological finds combined with a study of the Norse sagas enrich the understanding of Scandinavia's medieval past.

title: The Vikings
description:
S01 E02 — Land and People of Medieval Scandinavia
Scandinavia's landscape shapes its culture; dense forestation leads to close-knit communities; woodworking and sailing are the key means of long-distance travel; harsh winters engender skill in cold-weather commute; the emergence of great halls.

title: The Vikings
description:
S01 E03 — Scandinavian Society in the Bronze Age
The physical evidence paints a picture of the Bronze Age in Scandinavia; Viking ancestors trade Arctic goods, amber and slaves in exchange for foreign copper and tin; new wealth fosters larger villages; the beginnings of the Norse pantheon.

title: The Vikings
description:
S01 E04 — Scandinavia in the Celtic and Roman Ages
Scandinavia survives on trade with the Celts; contact with Rome enriches the upper classes; Scandinavians returning from Roman military service bring back advanced weapons and armor; petty kings and the first Scandinavian sailing ships emerge.

title: Cities of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E01 — The Lure of the City
Cities are integral to modern lives; why wandering ancient humans leave the forests and plains to create settlements; the fundamental question of "why" is the first step toward understanding the inhabitants and lessons from ancient cities.

title: Cities of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E02 — Çatalhöyük - First Experiment in Urban Living
Imagining a city with no streets, public buildings or common spaces; the world's first city offers an intriguing window into life in the Neolithic era; exploring the remains of Çatalhöyük's family housing, murals and religious shrines.

title: Cities of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E03 — Jericho and Its Walls
The story of the walls of Jericho in the Book of Joshua; looking past the biblical story; what architectural remains suggest about Jericho, whose ritual spaces help create a community and whose walls help define the urban environment.

title: Cities of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E04 — Uruk - City of Gilgamesh
Looking at one of the most marvelous cities in the ancient world; Uruk exhibits many of the hallmarks of ancient civilization; division of labor among its craftsmen; a class hierarchy that includes professional priests; records of art and literature.

title: Late Antiquity: Crisis and Transformation
description:
S01 E01 — The World of Late Antiquity
Exploring the origin of the term late antiquity; why this historical view better reflects the period from the third to the eighth centuries than the traditional view that Rome has a decline and fall; the major themes and issues of the course.

title: Late Antiquity: Crisis and Transformation
description:
S01 E02 — The Crisis of the 3rd Century
The crisis of the third century, when Rome finds its frontiers threatened on several fronts; armies make and unmake emperors with alarming regularity; the literature of the period also reveals unmistakable feelings of despair and uncertainty.

title: Late Antiquity: Crisis and Transformation
description:
S01 E03 — The New Empire of Diocletian
No one predicts that Rome is about to raise two of its greatest rulers, Diocletian and Constantine; Diocletian institutes a series of reforms that divide the empire into east and west; launching the last and fiercest persecution of Christians.

title: Late Antiquity: Crisis and Transformation
description:
S01 E04 — Constantine's Roman Revolution
Turning to Constantine; how he extends Diocletian's reforms; among them, he gives the empire a new capital at Byzantium, which he renames Constantinople after himself; he also takes the surprising step of legalizing Christianity.

title: Conquest of the Americas
description:
S01 E01 — Three Peoples Collide
Neither the Eurocentric term 'discovery' nor the blandly neutral 'encounters' do justice to the impact of Europeans, Africans and Native Americans coming together in the New World; a collision whose causes and effects are outlined in this lecture.

title: Conquest of the Americas
description:
S01 E02 — The Native Americans
Most of the inhabitants of the Americas arrive in migratory waves from Asia between 40,000 and 2,000 B.C.; their civilizations are based on sophisticated irrigation and farming; complex religions and social structures; rivaling those of Europe.

title: Conquest of the Americas
description:
S01 E03 — Mayas, Aztecs, and Incas
The Aztecs and Incas create empires built upon religions of conquest; powered by the control of water, around Lake Texcoco in Mexico and high in the Andes Mountains, respectively; the Maya develops an advanced knowledge of astronomy and mathematics.

title: Conquest of the Americas
description:
S01 E04 — Europeans and Africans
Europe and Africa are connected for centuries by Old World trading networks centered around the Mediterranean; in the 15th century, Spain and Portugal shift the trade out of the Mediterranean and into the Atlantic, along the west coast of Africa.

title: America After the Cold War: The First 30 Years
description:
S01 E01 — 1990: America's New World Order
The end of the Cold War is a key point in history; the rapid collapse of the Soviet Union; the fall of the Berlin Wall; delving into the American story in the early 1990s; conflicts in Kuwait and Bosnia test America's new role in a post-Soviet world.

title: America After the Cold War: The First 30 Years
description:
S01 E02 — The Clintons and the 1990s
Bill Clinton's presidency dominates the domestic news in the 1990s. From his dramatic showdown with Newt Gingrich and the Republican Congress's Contract with America, this is a presidency of high drama; surveying the tumultuous decade.

title: America After the Cold War: The First 30 Years
description:
S01 E03 — A New Millennium, George W. Bush, and 9/11
The end of the Cold War may have reshaped the world order, but 9/11 and the subsequent war on terror changes America; tracing the events leading up to the terrorist attack on American soil on Sept. 11, 2001; learning why 19 hijackers attack America.

title: America After the Cold War: The First 30 Years
description:
S01 E04 — The US Wars in Afghanistan and Iraq
Historians discuss and debate the wars in Afghanistan and Iraq; the war in Afghanistan has some justification, given the role of Al-Qaeda in 9/11; Professor Allitt reviews the facts surrounding the war in Iraq; the war's effect on the United States.

title: Tocqueville and the American Experiment
description:
S01 E01 — An Overview of Democracy in America
The course begins with a brief overview of Tocqueville's masterwork; written to educate the French about democracy; it is originally published as two separate volumes, released five years apart.

title: Tocqueville and the American Experiment
description:
S01 E02 — Alexis de Tocqueville-A Brief Biography
William R. Cook introduces the young French nobleman, trained as a lawyer; his most famous book is only one achievement in a life marked by several; service as France's foreign minister; a history of the French Revolution regarded as a classic.

title: Tocqueville and the American Experiment
description:
S01 E03 — The Journey to America
Tocqueville rarely describes specific events or conversations; his letters and journals allow one to follow him on his trip; getting an excellent feel for the experiences he and his colleague, Gustave de Beaumont, have in America.

title: Tocqueville and the American Experiment
description:
S01 E04 — Equality of Conditions and Freedom
This lecture considers the meaning and implications of what Tocqueville introduces in the first paragraph of "Democracy in America"; the foundation of the democratic enterprise; the concept he calls equality of conditions.

title: America in the Gilded Age and Progressive Era
description:
S01 E01 — 1865: "Bind Up the Nation's Wounds"
The key historical forces that characterize the Gilded Age and the Progressive Era; the competing ideals that define these eras; the US in 1865; the extraordinary social, political and economic changes unleashed by the devastation of the Civil War.

title: America in the Gilded Age and Progressive Era
description:
S01 E02 — The Reconstruction Revolution
The Reconstruction era following the Civil War; governmental policies and legislation enacted to safeguard the welfare of former slaves and average citizens; these policies are progressively dismantled, the South comes under the rule of the whites.

title: America in the Gilded Age and Progressive Era
description:
S01 E03 — Buffalo Bill Cody and the Myth of the West
The story of the conquest of the American West; key myths surrounding the West and how it is settled; the motives and realities of westward migration; the components of the western economy; the conflicts with Native Americans that lead to violence.

title: America in the Gilded Age and Progressive Era
description:
S01 E04 — Smokestack Nation: The Industrial Titans
America rises from a developing nation status in 1865 to become a great industrial power by 1900; the unfolding of the American industrial revolution; the advent of big business in the railroad, steel and oil industries; consumerism and advertising.
